title: From Nagavalli to Vasu Annan: Malayalam film characters take over AI reels
source_used: The New Indian Express (pre-fetched full text)
key_facts: The New Indian Express reports a trend among Malayali (Kerala) social-media users: AI-made videos of popular Malayalam film characters such as Nagavalli, Vasu Annan, Digambaran, Dashamoolam Damu and Kodumon Potti dancing or battling to rap and electro-pop tracks.

It began as a playful rivalry between fan pages of actors, including Chemban Vinod as 'Copper_V' and Ambika Mohan as 'Ambaddie', with a third camp around actor K Rajesh Hebbar; AI creators then turned the rivalry into videos.
An AI video of Kannan Srank, Vasu Annan and Dashamoolam Damu to a loop from Akcent's 'Stay With Me' has over 450,000 views; some Nagavalli reels have passed a million views.

Graphic designer Hari Krishna, who began with AI about a year ago using tools including Magnific and Higgsfield AI, makes viral videos such as four Fahadh Faasil characters in a car sing-along, and says the platforms cost a lot to use.

Fans such as lawyer Jissmon Joseph enjoy the videos as light relief; techie Nithin Varghese says some are over-exaggerated attention-grabbers; research scholar Sreenanda G says she is tired of too many AI trends.
The article is a feature built on interviews, with no overall data on how widespread the trend is.
quote_evidence: An AI video of Kannan Srank, Vasu Annan and Dashamoolam Damu vibing to a loop from Akcent’s ‘Stay With Me’ has clocked over 450,000 views.
Some Nagavalli reels have crossed a million views.
What began as a playful rivalry between fan pages soon became raw material for wacky AI videos.
why_it_matters_hint: It shows AI video tools turning local film fandom into fast-spreading memes, with viewers split between amusement and fatigue.
event_date: Published 10 Oct 2026; the trend is described as current, with no start date given.
notes: Feature article built on a few interviews; view counts are the paper's figures for individual videos. Characters and actors named are as the article spells them.
